content.text:
{"action":"finish","answer":"I can only cover the hardware part of this ticket, and I cannot finish the whole task from here.

1) School portal login (account issue): Not handled. I have no account or portal access, so I cannot check whether the account is active, locked, or expired, or reset it. This needs an agent with account access. I also cannot confirm with Help desk that someone has picked it up, or update the user. Please escalate this to Help desk or an accounts-capable agent.

2) Slow laptop (hardware check). Steps the student can try now:
- Restart the laptop and wait 2 minutes before opening apps.
- Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc). Check CPU, Memory, and Disk. If Disk stays near 100%, or Memory is above 90% with little running, note which process is using it.
- Check free space on the system drive. Keep at least 15% free.
- Check for overheating: the fan should be audible, and the bottom should not be very hot. Dust in vents can cause throttling.
- Check Settings > System > Storage for large files, and remove startup apps you do not need (Task Manager > Startup).
- If the disk is an older hard drive (HDD) and Disk usage stays high, or the drive makes clicking noises, it is likely a hardware fault. Back up the data and report it to IT for repair or replacement.
- Run Windows Memory Diagnostic if you see random crashes.

If these steps do not fix it, send the results (CPU, memory, disk percentages, free space, and drive type) to IT support for hardware repair.

Next step: Help desk must assign the login issue to an accounts-capable agent and tell the user when it is resolved."}

about.title: Handoff: a path through four agents
about.author: Agent Atlas Academy
about.description:
Two problems in one question: control may pass through several agents, and each sees only the note and the task.

**What it teaches**

A poor note starves the next agent, and a path with many handoffs can lose the second problem.

**What to watch**

Which problem each agent solves, and whether the second problem is ever answered.

Read more: [Handoff](#/learn/handoff)
